title: Three-Node Graph Routing Simulation: conserved-message ledger with an optional shortcut edge
description:
A small, dependency-free Python discrete-event simulation that compares a three-node message-routing graph with and without an optional bidirectional M1-M3 shortcut, under a matched capacity and loss budget.

Each directed edge has its own capacity, latency and deterministic loss quota. Every tick asserts the conserved-message ledger (change in inventory = injections - absorptions - losses). The tool reports delivery by deadline, conditional latency, undelivered messages, backlog and losses, and includes a stress sweep across offered rates.

Scope: a graph-routing analogy only. The 'white-hole-like', 'black-hole-like' and 'wormhole-like' labels refer to injection, absorption and the optional edge; the code does not model general relativity, spacetime, physical membranes or any OES32 feature. All results are SYNTHETIC.

Python 3.10+, standard library only. 11 unittest tests and the stress sweep run in GitHub Actions. License: AGPL-3.0-only.
